Federal Parliament
House of Representatives, 2082
Second Session
Meeting Number - 24
Nepal
Notice Paper - 2
(Brief Minutes of the Meeting Proceedings)
Wednesday, Ashadh 3, 2083
The meeting of the House of Representatives today commenced at 11:10 AM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal.
At the beginning of the meeting, when the Honourable Members from Nepali Congress, CPN (UML), Nepal Communist Party, Shram Sanskriti Party, and Rastriya Prajatantra Party stood up in front of their seats and requested time to speak, the Right Honourable Speaker granted them time. The Honourable Members expressed their views on issues such as the government immediately providing relief and resettlement to the landless squatters displaced by the "Dozar" terror, the protest will continue until the Prime Minister corrects his statement on border issues made in Parliament, the Speaker, who is supposed to be the guardian of the House, has not been able to sever ties with Rastriya Prajatantra Party, and the Prime Minister and Ministers are accountable to the House as per Article 76, Sub-article 10 of the Constitution.
Honourable Harkaraj Rai
Honourable Chandra Mohan Yadav

Meanwhile, after Honourable Gopal Sharma finished speaking, Honourable Lal Vikram Thapa raised a point of order, stating that the word "arojak" (anarchic) used by the speaker Honourable Member towards the Prime Minister and the words used by Honourable Ganesh Karki after Honourable Chandra Mohan Yadav finished speaking, were in violation of Rule 21(b) of the Regulations, and should be removed from the parliamentary records. The Right Honourable Speaker drew the attention of the Honourable Members to Rule 21, Clause (b) of the Regulations.
During the impromptu session that followed, the following Honourable Members expressed their views: State investment should be made only after determining the age of the current fiscal year; the allocated budget is not balanced; scientific surveys of the country's hydropower production capacity and potential should be conducted; the instruction given to facilitate the supply of medicines for cancer patients has not been effective, and the government should intensify its monitoring; the problems of tea industrialists and farmers should be addressed; the issues of the women protesting at Maitighar should be heard; the Nepali women who went for foreign employment in Kuwait but are in Kuwaiti jails and stranded should be immediately rescued; although the project under construction by a private entity in Sankhuwasabha benefits electricity and irrigation, it has directly impacted the local economy and damaged natural resources; the government's courageous step to remove squatters has turned into recklessness due to the death of Indrabahadur Rai, Rabin Tamang and Ravi Tamang's wife, and Bhojraj Darji during treatment; the driver driving recklessly in Morang, causing the death of Indrabahadur Shrestha, should be punished; 90 percent of women MPs are also affected by cyberbullying, and cyberbullying incidents should be controlled; the bridge under construction over the Beni River in Gurmakot, Surkhet, should be completed on time; the Chaite paddy planted in Tripurasundari Rural Municipality, Dadeldhura, is affected by a disease called Neck Blight, and it should be controlled; Dharmabahadur Rai and Ral Bahadur Rai, residents of Manahari Rural Municipality, Makwanpur, were injured in a bear attack while grazing buffaloes, and budget should be allocated for the management of human-wildlife conflict and control of monkeys and wild boars; the government's attention should be drawn to the provision of proper health treatment at Okhaldhunga District Hospital; citizens in various districts have to face great risk daily due to the lack of roads, and the government should allocate the necessary budget for physical infrastructure; the supply of chemical fertilizers for farmers in various districts should be ensured; hospitals operating without renewing their registration should be regulated, and labour exploitation of health workers should be investigated and the guilty punished; the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation should pay attention to the incident where the "Work for Peace" team, traveling with a message of world peace, was denied flight permission by Air India while en route to Delhi; the participation of the Nepali women's national football team in the 20th Asian Games should be ensured; an environment should be created to watch the World Cup Football competition for free on national television; the government should address the issue of land possession by farmers in Parshuram, Dadeldhura, which has been restricted by the District Forest Office, leaving the future of 400 farmers uncertain; the Prime Minister's statement on border issues should be removed from parliamentary records; the government's stance on past political movements should be clarified; the National Medical Education Commission meeting chaired by the Prime Minister passed related procedures, and individuals not recognized by law should not be present as Vice-Chairperson; seven girl students fell ill at Manpur Secondary School in Bardiya, forcing the school to close, and the government should address this; Aryan Singh, a grade 12 student at DAV College, Lalitpur, recently committed suicide, and the government should implement mental health awareness programs.
Honourable Narendra Kumar Karki

Meanwhile, Honourable Indira Rana raised a point of order during Honourable Yeshoda Kumari Baral's speech, stating that the word "chhadatantra" (anarchy) used should be removed from the parliamentary records.
Thereafter, the Right Honourable Speaker informed that there was no Zero Hour or Special Time scheduled for today.
Subsequently, the Honourable Minister for Youth, Employment and Labour, Ramji Yadav, responded to the questions raised during the discussion on the budget allocation titles related to the Ministry of Youth, Employment and Labour. Furthermore, regarding the clarification sought by Honourable Harkaraj Rai and Honourable Aaren Rai concerning the response, the Honourable Minister for Youth, Employment and Labour, Ramji Yadav, provided further clarification.
Thereafter, the Honourable Minister for Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Gauri Kumari, responded to the questions raised during the discussion on the budget allocation titles related to the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies. Furthermore, concerning the clarification sought by the following Honourable Members regarding the response, the Honourable Minister for Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Gauri Kumari, provided clarification.

After the Honourable Minister for Industry finished her response, Honourable Harkaraj Rai stood up in front of his seat, demanding clarification as he had not received a response to his query, and requested to be allowed to seek clarification. Although the Right Honourable Speaker repeatedly urged him not to debate, stating that clarification on clarification is not allowed, he remained standing.
Meanwhile, Honourable Manish Jha raised a point of order, stating that as per Rule 54 and 55 of the Regulations, there is no provision for a minister to provide clarification on clarification. Similarly, Honourable Dhuvraj Rai, citing Rule 44 of the Regulations, expressed that discussions on the issue of nationality should not be against the national interest and requested a study of the Regulations.
Thereafter, the Honourable Minister for Agriculture, Forests and Environment, Gita Chaudhary, responded to the questions raised during the discussion on the budget allocation titles related to the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment. Furthermore, concerning the clarification sought by the following Honourable Members regarding the response, the Honourable Minister for Agriculture, Forests and Environment, Gita Chaudhary, provided clarification.
Honourable Jog Kumar Barbariya Yadav
Honourable Prakash Pathak

Subsequently, the Honourable Minister for Communications and Information Technology, Dr. Bikram Timilsina, responded to the questions raised during the discussion on the budget allocation titles related to the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology.
After that, the meeting of the House of Representatives was adjourned for 15 minutes today at 2:25 PM.
The meeting of the House of Representatives, which was adjourned for 15 minutes today, commenced at 3:15 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal.
First, after the Honourable Members from the Shram Sanskriti Party stood up in front of their seats, the Right Honourable Speaker informed them that the matter for which the Honourable Member sought a response from the Honourable Minister could be asked by submitting a written question to the concerned Honourable Minister as per Chapter 8 of the Regulations, after which the Honourable Members took their seats.
Subsequently, regarding the response of the Honourable Minister for Communications and Information Technology, Dr. Bikram Timilsina, the Honourable Minister for Communications and Information Technology, Dr. Bikram Timilsina, provided further clarification concerning the clarification sought by Honourable Sarita Lama and Honourable Harkaraj Rai.
Thereafter, the Honourable Minister for Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, Khadga Raj Paudel, responded to the questions raised during the discussion on the budget allocation titles related to the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation. Furthermore, concerning the clarification sought by Honourable Sarita Lama and Honourable Harkaraj Rai regarding the response, the Honourable Minister for Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, Khadga Raj Paudel, provided clarification.
Subsequently, the Honourable Minister for Health and Food Security, Nisha Mehta, responded to the questions raised during the discussion on the budget allocation titles related to the Ministry of Health and Food Security. Furthermore, concerning the clarification sought by the following Honourable Members regarding the response, the Honourable Minister for Health and Food Security, Nisha Mehta, provided clarification.
Honourable Narendra Kumar Karki
Honourable Harkaraj Rai
3.

Honourable Bhim Kumari Budhamagar
Honourable Tahir Ali Bhat

Thereafter, Honourable Madan Krishna Shrestha took impromptu time and drew the government's attention to human organ transplantation and donation. Similarly, Honourable Janu Poudyal stated that Bimal Khatri tragically died after being swept away by a sudden flood while returning from studying at Janata Primary School in Nau Bahini Rural Municipality, Pyuthan, and Milan Khatri is missing, and the Government of Nepal should conduct a search as soon as possible.
Subsequently, the Honourable Minister for Land Management, Cooperatives, and Poverty Alleviation, Pratibha Rawal, responded to the questions raised during the discussion on the budget allocation titles related to the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, and Poverty Alleviation. Furthermore, concerning the clarification sought by Honourable Harkaraj Rai and Honourable Narendra Kumar Karki regarding the response, the Honourable Minister for Land Management, Cooperatives, and Poverty Alleviation, Pratibha Rawal, provided clarification.
Thereafter, the Honourable Minister for Women, Children, Senior Citizens and Social Welfare, Sita Badi, responded to the questions raised during the discussion on the budget allocation titles related to the Ministry of Women, Children, Senior Citizens and Social Welfare. Furthermore, concerning the clarification sought by Honourable Narendra Kumar Karki and Honourable Yeshoda Kumari Baral regarding the response, the Honourable Minister for Women, Children, Senior Citizens and Social Welfare, Sita Badi, provided clarification.
Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker informed that the responses to the questions raised during the discussion on the budget allocation titles under the Appropriation Bill, 2083, for the Ministry of Education and Sports, Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Ministry of Physical Infrastructure Development, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Defence, Prime Minister's Office, Office of the Vice President and Office of the Council of Ministers, National Planning Commission, and Office of the President would be provided by the respective ministers in the meeting scheduled for Ashadh 4, 2083.
Thereafter, the next meeting of the House of Representatives was adjourned today at 5:30 PM, to be held on Thursday, Ashadh 4, 2083, at 11:00 AM.
Padma Prasad Pandey
Secretary
